title: Request Anatomy Explorer — Debug Journey & Error Taxonomy Lens
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Design an interactive 'Request Anatomy Explorer' in Redwood Console that helps engineers triage failed or degraded requests by surfacing the execution path, retry chain, error taxonomy, and inspected payloads. The Explorer should let users navigate a single request's lifecycle (ingress -> routing -> model variant -> runtime kernels -> fallback) and reveal where errors, retries, or degraded latency occurred. This feature is intended for the Request Details page and should be available from failed-request list items and incident digests.
acceptance_criteria: Explorer is accessible from Request Details and Failed Requests list (click 'Open in Explorer').
Timeline view shows discrete request phases with duration and token counts (ingest, routing, model-infer, post-process).
Retry chain panel shows each attempt with status, timestamp, latency, and error code.
Error taxonomy lens maps raw error strings to user-facing categories with suggested remediation steps.
Payload inspector supports raw JSON view, pretty view, and redaction preview for PII.
Drilldowns link directly to related observability artifacts (trace, logs, PRD links, GitHub PRs) when available.
decisions: Single-panel master-detail layout chosen over modal stack to allow side-by-side timeline and payload inspection.
Error taxonomy will be client-side mapped first (v1) with opt-in server-side ML grouping later.
Default view opens on 'Timeline + Retry Chain'; payload inspector collapsed to reduce noise but expandable.
Use color+icon system for error severity (info/warning/error/critical) consistent with Console theme.
Start with static redaction previews; full KMS-backed redaction engines will be a later engineering task.
Interaction patterns should work with keyboard navigation and basic screen reader semantics (aria labels for timeline nodes).
tradeoffs: Showing both full payloads and timeline detail increases DOM size; we will implement lazy-loading panes to preserve performance.
Client-side taxonomy is fast but may misclassify edge-case messages; server-side grouping improves accuracy but requires infra work.
Embedding links to traces/logs improves triage speed but exposes more surface area for RBAC checks — Console will check route-level permissions before exposing links.
review_feedback: (2025-02-12) PM Sofia Ramirez: Love the taxonomy lens, ask to include 'business impact' badge when error maps to billing or quota issues.
(2025-02-13) Eng lead Amir Patel: Concern about loading full payloads for large requests; recommend byte-limit and 'load full' button.
(2025-02-15) Reliability Eng: Request to add an overlay that shows whether a retry was automatic (runtime) vs client-initiated for clearer ownership.
comments: 2025-02-11 Maya Chen: Created initial PRD and wireframes; uploaded to Figma and Confluence.
2025-02-12 Luca Moretti: Converted wireframes to high-fidelity comps; added timeline micro-interactions.
2025-02-14 Usability test: 5 engineers completed 15-min sessions. Key learning: users wanted 'copy error context' and quick link to 'replay request' in the runtime console.
2025-02-16 Design review: Decided to include error clustering hint on the timeline to denote repeated similar errors across retries.

2025-02-17 Eng sync: Agreed on lazy-loading payloads, backend flags for redaction previews, and an ENG task to expose runtime metadata (kernel selection, quantization mode). Linked ENG tasks in dependencies.
next_steps: Deliver handoff package to engineering (design tokens, interactions spec, accessible aria labels) by 2025-02-20.
Create a small A/B prototype to validate 'taxonomy vs raw message' usefulness in the field.
Add instrumentation checklist for telemetry (which timeline node emitted the error, which kernel, cache hit/miss).
Coordinate with Security for payload redaction UX and KMS flows.
